about: Insights from two learning notes by the Climate Centre for Cities (C-Cube), National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), with GIZ India and the International Climate Initiative (IKI), 2026, under the Urban Act project: Module 1, 'Cities and Climate Fundamentals Primer' (supplied by the owner as a link), and Module 2, 'Climate Change Adaptation Actions in Indian Cities'. They are training material for officials in Indian city governments, so what they say enters as guidance and NIUA's reading, never as evidence that a measure works. Module 1's heat figures are cited there to newspapers and are left out (see ledger.md). No individual is named. stage.js writes data/inbox/2026-11-niua-cities-climate/sources.json; verify-sources.yml checks each term on the publisher's own PDF or page; apply.js uses only confirmed claims.

claims.text: A series of four learning notes for officials in Indian city governments: climate fundamentals, adaptation actions, urban climate finance, and institutionalising climate action; the adaptation note covers resilience to heat, flooding and water stress.
rests_on: resilience to heat, flooding, water stress

claims.where: Practical guides on Cool by design, Greener, cooler cities and Cooling centres
claims.text: Learning note 2 shows a city how to report results by pairing what it builds (an output, such as the number of roofs treated, hectares of green cover added or cooling centres created) with what changes for people (an outcome, such as lower indoor temperatures and less heat illness).
Heat stress varies from ward to ward: it is far greater in densely built areas with little vegetation.
rests_on: Heat vulnerability is not uniformly distributed
densely built areas with low vegetation

claims.text: Shade, tree cover and cool spaces designed without people in informal settlements in mind may do little for those most at risk.
rests_on: creating shaded areas, increasing tree cover

claims.text: NIUA's Climate Centre for Cities works with Indian cities on climate action; its heat work includes the Heat Resilient Cities Framework and a Building Heat Resilient Cities programme.
